questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to 3 − log x + 2 log y? (log means log base 10.)
options: log(3y²/x)
log(100y²/x)
log(1000y²/x)
log(1000 + y² − x)
questions.explanation: Write 3 as a log: 3 = log 1000, because 10³ = 1000. A coefficient becomes a power: 2 log y = log y². Adding logs multiplies the insides and subtracting divides: log 1000 + log y² − log x = log(1000y²/x). log(3y²/x) treats the 3 as log 3; log(100y²/x) uses log 100, which is 2, not 3; log(1000 + y² − x) adds and subtracts the insides instead of multiplying and dividing.

questions.stem: A 3-person crew is chosen from 5 men and 4 women. How many possible crews include at least one woman?
questions.explanation: Total crews: C(9,3) = 84. Crews with no women (all men): C(5,3) = 10. At least one woman: 84 − 10 = 74. 84 is every crew; 112 picks 'one woman' first (4 ways) then any 2 of the other 8 (28 ways), which counts crews with 2 or 3 women more than once; 40 counts exactly one woman only (4 × C(5,2)).

questions.stem: The supplement of an angle is 12° more than 4 times its complement. What is the angle?
questions.explanation: Supplement = 180 − x and complement = 90 − x. So 180 − x = 4(90 − x) + 12 → 180 − x = 372 − 4x → 3x = 192 → x = 64°. Check: supplement 116°, complement 26°, and 4 × 26 + 12 = 116 ✓. 60° drops the +12; 56° subtracts the 12 ('12 more' means add); 26° is the complement, not the angle.

questions.stem: One root of x² − kx + 10 = 0 is 3 more than the other. If k > 0, what is k?
questions.explanation: Call the roots r and r + 3. Their product is the constant term: r(r + 3) = 10 → r² + 3r − 10 = 0 → (r + 5)(r − 2) = 0. With k > 0, r = 2, so the roots are 2 and 5 and k = their sum = 7. (Shortcut: k² = (difference)² + 4 × product = 9 + 40 = 49.) Check: x² − 7x + 10 = (x − 2)(x − 5) ✓. √29 uses 9 + 2 × 10 instead of 9 + 4 × 10; 13 adds the gap and the product; 10 is the product of the roots, not the sum.

questions.stem: Which statement can be inferred only from the passage?
options: Contractor personnel must follow every command safety instruction while working at the command.
Personnel on temporary additional duty are exempt from command safety instructions.
A visitor who has been briefed on a work area's hazards may enter it without an escort.
Whether a contractor is bound by a particular safety instruction depends on the terms of the contract.
questions.passage: Command safety instructions apply to all military and civilian personnel assigned to the command, including personnel on temporary additional duty. Contractor personnel are bound by these instructions only to the extent specified in their contracts. Visitors shall be briefed on the hazards of any work area they enter and shall be escorted while in that area.
questions.explanation: 'Contractor personnel are bound by these instructions only to the extent specified in their contracts' — the contract decides. 'Every instruction' over-claims beyond what a contract may specify; personnel on temporary additional duty are expressly INCLUDED, not exempt; and visitors must be briefed AND escorted, so the briefing does not replace the escort.

questions.stem: Which statement can be inferred only from the passage?
options: A phone that has been switched off may be carried into a space where classified information is processed.
All personal electronic devices are prohibited throughout the command.
A medical device with a transmitter is allowed in a classified space as long as it is switched off.
A member with a transmitter-equipped medical device might be allowed to bring it into a classified processing space.
questions.passage: Personal electronic devices may be carried in the command's general work spaces. In spaces designated for processing classified information, devices with cameras, microphones or wireless transmitters are prohibited, whether or not they are switched on. A medical device that contains a transmitter may be permitted in such a space with the written approval of the security manager.
questions.explanation: Such a medical device 'may be permitted… with the written approval of the security manager'. The prohibition applies 'whether or not they are switched on', which defeats both 'switched off' choices — the medical exception depends on approval, not on the power switch; and devices are allowed in general work spaces.

questions.stem: Which statement can be inferred only from the passage?
options: A safety stand-down is required within 30 days after every mishap.
The individuals involved in the mishap may not be mentioned during the stand-down.
Those involved may be discussed if needed to explain the sequence of events.
The stand-down must be held within 30 days, and its purpose is to establish who was at fault.
questions.passage: Commands shall conduct a safety stand-down within 30 days after any Class A mishap. The stand-down is intended to review the lessons of the mishap with all hands, not to assign blame; accordingly, discussion of the individuals involved shall be limited to what is necessary to explain the sequence of events.
questions.explanation: Discussion of the individuals is 'limited to what is necessary to explain the sequence of events', so it is allowed to that extent. The 30-day rule follows a 'Class A mishap', not every mishap; 'limited' is not a total ban; and the stand-down is 'not to assign blame' — the last choice reverses its purpose.

questions.stem: Which choice can be derived solely from the information in the passage?
options: Restriction imposed before a hearing is a form of punishment in itself.
Time spent on pre-hearing restriction must be deducted from any later punishment.
A restricted member chooses the times at which to muster with the duty officer.
Time already spent on restriction might lighten a member's later punishment.
questions.passage: A member placed on restriction shall not go beyond the limits specified in the restriction order and shall muster with the duty officer at the times the order sets. Restriction imposed before a hearing is not a punishment in itself; it is used to ensure the member's presence. Time spent on such pre-hearing restriction may be taken into account when punishment is later decided.
questions.explanation: Pre-hearing restriction time 'may be taken into account when punishment is later decided', so it can lighten the result. Pre-hearing restriction 'is not a punishment in itself' (reversed); 'may be taken into account' is not 'must be deducted' (over-claim); and the muster times are those 'the order sets'.

questions.stem: The open tank shown is filled with still water. At which marked point on the wall is the water pressure greatest?
options: Point A
Point C
Point B
It is the same at all three points, because it is the same water
questions.explanation: Pressure in a still liquid depends on depth below the surface (P = ρgh). C is deepest, so it has the most water pressing down from above and the highest pressure. The pressure is not equal throughout: that idea (Pascal's principle) applies to an extra pressure added to a sealed fluid, not to the weight of the fluid itself.

questions.stem: A 90 lb load hangs from a rigid bar held up by two vertical springs side by side, one with a stiffness of 20 lb/in and one of 10 lb/in. The load is positioned so that the bar hangs level. How much of the load does the stiffer spring carry?
options: 60 lb
45 lb
30 lb
90 lb
questions.explanation: A level bar means both springs stretch the same distance x. Together they give 20x + 10x = 30x = 90 lb, so x = 3 in. The stiffer spring carries 20 × 3 = 60 lb and the softer 10 × 3 = 30 lb. Equal stretch, unequal force: the stiffer spring takes the larger share, not half.

questions.stem: A screw jack, a wood screw and a driven-in doorstop wedge all hold their loads without slipping back when you let go. This is mainly because —
options: their ideal mechanical advantage is less than 1
they are made of harder material than the load
the load always acts straight down, never along the slope of the thread
friction is large enough to stop the load driving them backward
questions.explanation: In wedges and screws, the sliding surfaces are pressed together hard, so friction is very large compared with the small part of the load's force that acts along the slope. That friction stops the load from driving them backward. The same friction is why their efficiency is low. Their ideal MA is far ABOVE 1, not below it.

questions.stem: A sailor stands on the centerline of a long, straight, closed runway. A crash truck with its siren on drives straight toward her along the centerline at a steady speed, swerves around her at the last moment, and then drives straight away along the centerline at the same speed. Ignoring the brief swerve, compared with the siren's true pitch she hears —
options: a steady higher pitch as it approaches, then a steady lower pitch as it moves away
a pitch that rises steadily as it approaches, then falls steadily as it moves away
the true pitch throughout, only growing louder and then quieter
a steady lower pitch as it approaches, then a steady higher pitch as it moves away
questions.explanation: Because she is directly in the truck's path, its whole speed is toward her while it approaches, so each wave is emitted a little closer to her and the waves arrive bunched up: a higher frequency. Moving away, the waves are stretched out: a lower frequency. At a steady speed the shift stays the same, so the pitch does not keep rising as it gets nearer; what rises is the LOUDNESS. A steadily rising pitch confuses loudness with pitch; hearing the true pitch ignores the Doppler effect; and the last option has the shifts backward.

questions.stem: Movement of an airplane about its lateral axis is called ___ and is controlled mainly by the ___.
options: roll; ailerons
yaw; rudder
pitch; rudder
pitch; elevator
questions.explanation: The lateral axis runs wingtip to wingtip; rotation about it is pitch, controlled by the elevator (or stabilator). Roll is about the longitudinal axis (ailerons) and yaw is about the vertical axis (rudder).

questions.stem: Immediately after an engine failure in cruise, a helicopter pilot should first:
options: Raise the collective to stop the descent
Pull the cyclic fully aft to slow down
Lower the collective to maintain rotor RPM
Apply left pedal to counter the yaw
questions.explanation: Without power the blades' drag bleeds rotor RPM fast; lowering the collective flattens them so upward airflow keeps the rotor turning. With torque gone the nose yaws LEFT on a US design, so RIGHT pedal is needed.

questions.stem: A Navy jet takes on 1,200 gallons of JP-5. Using about 6.8 pounds per gallon, the fuel weighs about:
options: 7,200 pounds
9,000 pounds
8,160 pounds
10,020 pounds
questions.explanation: 1,200 × 6.8 = 8,160 lb. The distractors multiply by the avgas figure (6 → 7,200), the oil figure (7.5 → 9,000) and the water figure (8.35 → 10,020). JP-5, the Navy's high-flash-point shipboard fuel, is slightly denser than the 6.7 lb/gal planning figure for jet fuel.

questions.stem: Which change in conditions would usually help ADVECTION fog form and thicken, but would prevent or break up RADIATION fog?
options: The surface wind picking up from calm to about 25 knots
A clear sky through a long night
The surface wind picking up from calm to about 10 knots
The sun rising and heating the ground
questions.explanation: Radiation fog forms only in calm or nearly calm air, and a breeze mixes it out, while advection fog needs moist air to be moved over a colder surface, and winds up to about 15 knots let it form and thicken (FAA-H-8083-25, Chapter 12). At about 25 knots the wind is too strong even for advection fog, which lifts into low stratus. A clear sky through a long night favors radiation fog, not advection fog. Daytime heating burns off radiation fog but does nothing to thicken advection fog.
